body:
Allocator owner metadata and diagnostic call stacks store addresses in 32-bit values, and their Windows capture/allocation hooks use x86-only assembly. Carry pointer-width owner addresses from the allocation hook through allocator storage and reports; use 64-bit stack addresses through capture, collection and symbol lookup. Keep the legacy Win32 exported allocator owner type while selecting x64 return-address and context intrinsics.

The consumer closure includes Direct3d9/Headless allocation hooks, regex and DPVS allocation callbacks, RenderWorld leak diagnostics, Fatal/CallStack/CallStackCollector, and the existing DllExport allocator signature. DbgHelp uses the proper architecture context and thread handle, bypasses the demonstrated x64 function-table cache problem, and serializes the changed capture/lookup/minidump operations. Rebuild the affected allocator, debug, foundation, renderer/export and consumer modules together; diagnostic stack signatures/layouts also change on Win32.

This package is stacked on [allocator layout/order PR29](https://github.com/SWG-Source/client-tools/pull/29), exact base `2af9f19b502e9183731656cdaf93236faacb404e`. The [incremental comparison](https://github.com/Akilleez-QA/client-tools/compare/2af9f19b502e9183731656cdaf93236faacb404e...fc667f38eafbd4a2b4d50f96a31efb5cca3ef55c) contains three commits, **15 production files +346/-149**, with no new tests or build configuration. The master comparison also includes #29: five commits, 15 files, +352/−152. Merge or reconcile #29 first. The two preceding source commits replace existing Fatal/export-template breakpoint assembly with intrinsics; they are included source compatibility changes, not substitutes for build prerequisites. DllExport remains the existing import-library template, not a replacement runtime allocator.

Published [native checkpoint results](https://github.com/Akilleez-QA/client-tools/blob/f015ce7abc08d98902c6febdd50df204fe58137b/review/client-x64/allocator-math-next/RESULTS.md) report genuine v120 Debug/Release checks on both architectures: bounded DebugHelp capture/source/concurrency checks, allocator tracking observations and exact instruction-address comparisons for the five OsNewDel overloads. [DllExport and renderer-hook contract evidence](https://github.com/Akilleez-QA/client-tools/blob/f015ce7abc08d98902c6febdd50df204fe58137b/review/client-x64/allocator-math-next/dllexport-isolated-results.md) records four real project builds, unchanged 79-name Win32 export sets, and matching x64 allocation symbols. Candidate DebugHelp, DllExport and Direct3d9 hook source hashes match those records. These are historical integration-dependent results, not an exact isolated build of this restacked branch; no new build or runtime run occurred during packaging.

The historical build closure includes separately maintained common-header/imemmove changes, x64 project configuration, genuine STLport and SDK/provider inputs. Those are evidence prerequisites outside this source delta; this branch does not alone supply a complete x64 build. The callable source closure was checked, but final package qualification must retain that distinction.

Limits: address widening does not repair allocation-size overflow/counters or establish arbitrary allocator safety. The checkpoint retains the existing tracked `reallocate(NULL,16)` failure. Optional secondary owner-stack indices are not proven logical ancestors under optimization; [ordinary frame-order observations](https://github.com/Akilleez-QA/client-tools/blob/f015ce7abc08d98902c6febdd50df204fe58137b/review/client-x64/vendor-next/stack-owner-next/RESULTS.md) preserve eliminated/missing frames. Concurrent teardown, symbol unload/reload and minidump lifecycle are not qualified by the capture checks. This is not a fresh-master or full-runtime acceptance claim.
title: Preserve allocator owner and diagnostic stack addresses on Windows x64
